periods.analysis: At $11.99 in 2024-Q3, non-aeronautical revenue per enplanement is solidly green against the $10.50 target, giving Harborview International a healthy commercial cushion as summer leisure and cruise-transfer traffic stayed strong. The strongest lift came from garage yield management on the Blue and Long-Term decks, higher rental-car facility receipts, and the new digital advertising package on Concourse B gates 18-26. I like this result because it shows we are not simply waiting for airline rates to carry the airport; we are earning from the full passenger journey while keeping the terminal reliable.
periods.recommendations: Sustain the green result by keeping weekly price checks on parking products and protecting the high-performing Concourse B advertising inventory through the holiday booking window. Extend the BrightGate concessions pilot to two additional morning-bank locations, with a specific focus on mobile-order conversion and queue time under six minutes.

periods.analysis: Non-aeronautical revenue per enplanement rose to $12.50 in 2024-Q4, up $0.51 from $11.99, and remains comfortably green. Holiday travel, the Seaport Connector shuttle bundles, and stronger dwell time in the central marketplace all helped, but the disciplined piece was the commercial team holding premium parking inventory for peak departure banks rather than discounting early. The airport’s AA-rated financial posture is reflected here: steady passenger-facing revenue, diversified across concessions, parking, rental cars, and advertising, not one lucky line item.
periods.recommendations: Lock in the Q4 learning by making the peak-bank garage rules permanent for Thanksgiving through New Year and documenting the revenue impact by product code. Begin negotiations now with the top three central marketplace tenants for revised percentage-rent language before the 2025 summer schedule is finalized.

periods.analysis: The measure eased to $12.07 in 2025-Q1, down $0.43 from $12.50, but it remains green and still $1.57 above the $10.50 target. That step-down is consistent with the post-holiday travel mix and the January-February soft patch in rental-car days, not a structural weakness in the program. Dana Okonkwo’s rule at the airport is simple: a green number still deserves an autopsy, so staff traced the movement to lower premium garage occupancy on Tuesday-Wednesday departures and temporary construction screening around the Pier C coffee unit.
periods.recommendations: Keep the result green by retiming garage promotions toward shoulder-day business travelers instead of broad discounts that dilute yield. Finish the Pier C construction wayfinding package, including temporary blade signs at gates C7-C12, and require the vendor to report sales recovery weekly until the storefront is fully visible again.

periods.analysis: In 2025-Q2, non-aeronautical revenue per enplanement moved to $11.89, down $0.18 from $12.07, still green and well above target. The second consecutive decline is small but worth watching, especially because spring break volumes were good and should have supported stronger concessions capture. Staff identified two manageable drags: slower spend in the temporary food court near Checkpoint 3 and lower remote-lot utilization after the Route 9 airport express added frequency.
periods.recommendations: Sustain the green status by tightening the temporary food court offer: add one grab-and-go operator for the 5:30-8:00 a.m. bank and require point-of-sale reporting by concourse. Test bundled remote-lot pricing with Route 9 ticket validation for 60 days, so the city can capture value from the improved transit connection instead of letting it simply cannibalize parking revenue.

periods.analysis: The line turned back up in 2025-Q3 to $12.02, a $0.13 increase from $11.89, keeping the measure green and confirming the Q2 softness was manageable. Summer international traffic through Harborview’s coastal gateway helped duty-free and specialty retail, while the Port Welcome advertising buy added incremental revenue on the arrivals corridor screens. The important operational story is that concessions capture improved after the Checkpoint 3 temporary food court was rebalanced and mobile-order prompts were added to the airport app home screen.
periods.recommendations: Hold the momentum by extending the mobile-order prompts through all international arrival banks and tracking conversion separately for domestic and international passengers. Prepare the Q4 commercial plan now: reserve premium screen inventory for cruise, hospitality, and regional university campaigns, and keep the remote-lot bundle only if it remains revenue-positive per parked transaction.

periods.analysis: Non-aeronautical revenue per enplanement returned to $12.50 in 2025-Q4, up $0.48 from $12.02 and matching the prior holiday peak. That is a strong green result, and it shows the airport can repeat performance when the playbook is disciplined: premium garage controls, better marketplace visibility, and holiday advertising packages sold before the rush. The commercial engine is doing what a fast-growing hub needs it to do, funding service quality without leaning excessively on airline cost recovery.
periods.recommendations: Make the Q4 playbook a standing seasonal operating plan with named owners for parking yield, advertising closeout, and concession queue management. Extend the highest-performing Port Welcome screen package into a 2026 annual contract, but include make-good language tied to screen uptime so revenue growth does not outrun asset reliability.

periods.analysis: The measure settled to $12.24 in 2026-Q1, down $0.26 from $12.50, and remains green by a wide margin. This is the expected post-holiday moderation, but it is a better Q1 position than the airport had at the start of the arc, with stronger advertising commitments and more stable parking yield. The one watch-item is passenger spend during terminal works around the North Hall restroom renewal, where construction walls can quietly suppress retail capture if we do not manage paths and sightlines.
periods.recommendations: Sustain the green performance by assigning a commercial field check twice daily around the North Hall work zone, with photos of sightlines to units N4, N5, and the newsstand kiosk. Extend annual advertising packages to include shoulder-season tourism partners, and keep premium garage pricing rules in place rather than relaxing them during the March business-travel rebound.

periods.analysis: In 2026-Q2, non-aeronautical revenue per enplanement declined to $11.72, down $0.52 from $12.24, but it remains green and $1.22 above the $10.50 target. The size of the drop deserves attention even though the status is healthy: enplanements grew faster than commercial receipts, and the temporary closure of two Concourse A food units during ventilation work reduced spend per passenger. Parking also normalized after a strong Q1 business-travel period, with more travelers using curbside app-based drop-off and the expanded Route 9 express.
periods.recommendations: Keep the measure green by opening the Concourse A replacement carts before the next holiday bank, with lease terms that include minimum hours and percentage rent. Run a 90-day curbside-to-commerce campaign in the airport app that offers lounge, preorder food, and parking add-ons to travelers who are not using the garage. Report back next quarter on whether the $0.52 decline is a one-time construction and mode-shift effect or the start of a lower capture trend.

periods.analysis: Non-aeronautical revenue per enplanement eased from $11.72 to $11.55 but remains above the $10.50 target. The second consecutive decline warrants attention even while the result is green.
periods.recommendations: Check whether replacement concessions and parking offers are restoring spend per passenger; report the trend separately from passenger-volume growth.
